name: Tolterodine ER pivotal trial
question: In adults with overactive bladder and urge incontinence, how does once-daily tolterodine extended release compare with twice-daily immediate release and placebo?

design.population: 1,529 adults (81% women) with overactive-bladder symptoms for at least six months, at least eight micturitions per 24 hours, and five urge-incontinence episodes per week.
design.description: 167-center, double-blind, three-arm superiority randomized trial; electrocardiography assessed in 154 participants aged at least 65 years
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 415–416, and Table I; FDA medical review of protocol 98-TOCR-007, p 13 (phase)

verdictNote: Both formulations beat placebo on weekly incontinence; ER had less dry mouth than IR.
takeaway: In 1,529 adults randomized for 12 weeks, tolterodine ER 4 mg daily and IR 2 mg twice daily reduced weekly incontinence versus placebo (mean changes −11.8, −10.6, −6.9); ER had 18% greater median percentage reduction than IR and less dry mouth (118/505 versus 156/512).

reports.label: Randomized 12-week report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed 11248608, March 2001 issue; Crossref published date-parts [2001,3]
reports.citation: Van Kerrebroeck P, Kreder K, Jonas U, et al. "Tolterodine once-daily: superior efficacy and tolerability in the treatment of the overactive bladder." *Urology.* 2001;57(3):414-421. doi:10.1016/s0090-4295(00)01113-4

results.measure: Change in mean weekly episodes at 12 weeks

values.pbo: −6.9 ± 15.4 episodes/week (ITT n=507 with diary data; 508 randomized)

results.note: Mean changes ± SD; ITT with last observation carried forward. Effect is ER versus placebo 97.5% Bonferroni-adjusted CI; adjusted point estimate not printed. IR versus placebo 97.5% CI −6.0 to −1.3, P = 0.0005. The ER-versus-IR 18% relative improvement (P < 0.05) derives from the separate median percentage-change analysis.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 416, and Table II, p 417

results.measure: Median percentage reduction from baseline at 12 weeks
results.note: The ER-versus-IR median percentage-change comparison was 18% relative improvement (P < 0.05); the placebo significance tests concern mean changes.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 416, and Fig. 1, p 417

results.note: Effect is ER versus placebo 95% CI; IR versus placebo CI −0.9 to −0.1, P = 0.0079. Other diary variables were analyzed descriptively.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 416, and Table II, p 417

results.measure: Mean change ± SD in mL at 12 weeks
results.note: Effect is ER versus placebo 95% CI; IR versus placebo CI 10 to 21, P = 0.0001.
Effect is ER versus placebo 95% CI; IR versus placebo CI −0.5 to −0.1, P = 0.0035.

harms.label: Dry mouth, any severity
harms.locator: Full text, Table III, p 418, and Results, p 417
harms.note: ER dry-mouth frequency was reported as 23% lower relative to IR (P < 0.02); denominators are treated safety populations.

harms.label: Severe dry mouth

values.er: 1.8% (treated ER safety n=505; count not printed)

harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 417, and Fig. 3, p 418
harms.note: The text reports the percentage but no severe-event numerator or comparator percentages.

harms.label: Treatment withdrawal
harms.note: Counts are adverse-event withdrawals among randomized participants; overall premature withdrawals were 187/1,529 (12%).

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: Serious events led to early withdrawal in 1, 5, and 8 participants, respectively; none was considered treatment related.

delivery.label: Diary run-in
delivery.value: One- to two-week washout/run-in with seven consecutive diary days to confirm eligibility.

delivery.label: Randomized treatment

values.er: oral ER capsule 4 mg once daily for 12 weeks
values.ir: oral IR tablet 2 mg twice daily for 12 weeks

delivery.locator: Full text, Study design and Results, pp 415–416
delivery.note: Double-dummy masking; no dose adjustment; approximately 95% had acceptable pill-count compliance.

reports.label: 12-month open-label extension
reports.dateLocator: PubMed 12074774, June 2002 issue; Crossref published date-parts [2002,6]
reports.citation: Kreder K, Mayne C, Jonas U. "Long-term safety, tolerability and efficacy of extended-release tolterodine in the treatment of overactive bladder." *Eur Urol.* 2002;41(6):588-595. doi:10.1016/s0302-2838(02)00177-x
reports.followUp: 12 months of open-label ER treatment after the randomized phase

results.measure: Median percentage reduction from original randomized baseline among 759 extension completers at 12 months

values.er: 83.1% reduction (759 completers; diary-evaluable count not reported)

results.note: All entrants received ER regardless of prior randomized assignment; this is a completer analysis without imputation, not a randomized comparison.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 589–590, and Table 3, p 592

results.measure: Median percentage reduction from original randomized baseline among 759 extension completers at 12 months

values.er: 21.3% reduction (759 completers; diary-evaluable count not reported)

results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 590, and Table 3, p 592

results.measure: Median percentage increase from original randomized baseline among 759 extension completers at 12 months

values.er: 25.4% increase (759 completers; diary-evaluable count not reported)

results.endpoint: Patient perception of bladder condition and urgency
results.measure: Percentage reporting improvement after 12 months among extension completers

values.er: 75% bladder condition; 51% urgency (759 completers; response-specific denominators not printed)

harms.label: Acute urinary retention during extension
harms.note: Both retention cases were serious adverse events considered related to treatment.

harms.label: Serious adverse events during extension
harms.note: Twelve withdrew after a serious event; four events in three patients were considered related to tolterodine.

delivery.label: Extension entry and completion
delivery.value: 1,077 entered open-label ER 4 mg daily (368 prior ER, 370 prior IR, 339 prior placebo); 1,075 received treatment, and 759/1,075 (70.6%) completed 12 months.
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, p 589, and Results, pp 590–592
delivery.note: Prior-phase completers conflict within the report: 1,377 in the abstract (giving 78% entry) versus 1,337 in Results (giving 80.6%); no reconciled denominator is available. Among 1,075 treated, 107 discontinued for adverse events and 108 for lack of efficacy. More than 85% of 759 completers took at least 75% of medication by pill count; exact adherent numerator is unreported. No dose reduction was allowed.

results.note: Prespecified primary HRQoL domain in this secondary report; lower score is better. Effect is adjusted ER minus placebo, not the subtraction of displayed unadjusted changes.
